stem.text: Let f and g be continuous functions with \( \int_{2}^{10} f(x)\,dx = 11 \), \( \int_{4}^{10} f(x)\,dx = 6 \), and \( \int_{4}^{2} g(x)\,dx = 3 \). Find the value of \( \int_{2}^{4} \left(-2f(x) + g(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of g: \( \int_{2}^{4} g(x)\,dx = -(3) = -3 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.A: given integral of g from 4 to 2 used as if it ran from 2 to 4
distractor_derivations.B: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of f from 2 to 4 as 6 - (11)
distractor_derivations.C: integral of f from 10 to 4 taken as 6 instead of -6
